claims.text: cluster-review-checklist.md is for changes reaching past one service; each question points at the check or decision that answers it; a question with no check is checked by the reviewer; service code uses backend-review-checklist.md; automated checks are listed in fitness-functions.md.

Triggers: new CRD/operator; namespace for a new team; new cluster/environment; upgrade of Kubernetes or an add-on; new way changes reach the cluster. An edit in one service's overlay needs no review. The HPA example edits only api's production manifests (no trigger), yet the last section reviews it.
The checklist has six groups: workloads and resources; isolation and access; data and backups; upgrades and add-ons; cost; how changes reach the cluster; then a worked example.

Workload group: requests on every container (cluster-cost.md; reviewer checks); probes /health/live, /health/ready and security context like api (golden path template); image by digest (require-image-digest); schema validity (kubeconform in CI job manifests).

kube-scheduler places a Pod on a node by the sum of the requests of the Pods there, not by their actual use; a container that sets neither a request nor a limit (and gets no default from an admission mechanism such as a LimitRange) adds nothing to that sum.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Resource Management for Pods and Containers > How Pods with resource requests are scheduled

claims.text: require-image-digest: ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, failurePolicy Fail, on Pod CREATE/UPDATE; expression rejects images starting with ghcr.io/duyan11110/ that lack @sha256:; binding validationActions Deny, namespaceSelector kubernetes.io/metadata.name: donhang.

The Argo CD Application policies-staging applies platform/policies (staging's admission policies) with automated sync, selfHeal and prune; no other Application under apps/ applies platform/policies at stage-4, so production has no digest policy.

A ValidatingAdmissionPolicy acts through a ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding, which scopes it (matchResources) and sets validationActions such as Deny; a Pod outside the binding's namespaceSelector is not checked. Pod Security Admission enforces a namespace's Pod Security labels.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Validating Admission Policy > Creating a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (matchResources, namespaceSelector)

claims.text: The OpenTofu module donhang-platform creates only namespace donhang and sets its Pod Security labels: enforce from the environment's variable, warn and audit at restricted; a namespace created from the config repository gets no labels from it.

Decisions the checklist points at: ADR 0021 (encryption inside the cluster: not yet, with when to reopen), ADR 0020 (defines RTO and RPO as what the DR drill measures, not targets), ADR 0022 (provider lock-in points), ADR 0006 (SealedSecret), ADR 0019 (release), ADR 0023 (keys in the key service).

Checklist: a kubectl change outside Git is reverted by self-heal or stays unknown; an operator with no upgrade owner blocks the next Kubernetes upgrade; a backup never restored is not a backup. self-run-components.md names Argo CD and the ingress controller as in-cluster components.

Isolation group: Pod Security labels (OpenTofu platform layer); NetworkPolicy for ingress and egress (reviewer checks); ServiceAccount token or automountServiceAccountToken: false; encryption inside the cluster (ADR 0021).

Upgrades group: owner of each operator/add-on upgrade written in self-run-components.md; add-on runs on the cluster's Kubernetes version and the next one; multi-replica workloads have a PodDisruptionBudget so node upgrades do not remove all Pods at once.
At stage-4 envs/production/api.yaml sets replicas: 3; ADR 0022 moves production to a provider's managed Kubernetes.

Worked example: replicas removed from api in Git; maxReplicas bounded so api Pods x connections per Pod stays under PostgreSQL max_connections (capacity-plan.md); more nodes do not raise it; minReplicas >= 2; a PDB keeps one Pod; CPU request unchanged; checked only on the managed cluster.

Argo CD docs advise not tracking replicas in Git when an HPA manages them; with replicas in Git, the HPA's live value differs from Git and a sync applies Git's (the checklist's reason). Self-heal acts only on resources an Application manages; an object not in Git is tracked by none.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Diffing / Best Practices (leaving room for imperativeness, HPA and replicas)

claims.text: capacity-plan.md: each api Pod holds a Npgsql pool for ConnectionStrings:Default at default size; Payments, Notifications, migrations and backup jobs connect to the same server; total Pods x max connections per Pod of every service must stay below max_connections, read with SHOW max_connections.
PostgreSQL's max_connections is the server's limit on concurrent connections, and SHOW max_connections prints its current value.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: Server Configuration > Connections and Authentication (max_connections); SQL Commands > SHOW

claims.text: An HPA with a CPU Utilization target compares measured CPU as a percentage of the containers' CPU request, so changing the request changes the point at which it scales.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Horizontal Pod Autoscaling > Algorithm details; k8s.l4.horizontal-pod-autoscaler summary line 1

claims.text: kubeconform checks manifests against Kubernetes' schema; resources and requests are optional fields of a container, so a container with no requests passes it.
claims.source_hint: kubeconform README; Kubernetes API reference: Container > resources (optional)

claims.text: Lab clusters at stage-4 run no metrics-server, so the HPA worked example cannot be checked there.

Opinion (trade-offs): reviewing only cluster-level changes against touched groups costs less than a full review per edit, which tends toward skimming; checks alone miss what no check tests or where none runs.

Opinion (choices): an api memory-limit edit in the staging overlay needs only code review; a new team namespace starts with isolation then workload questions by hand; a Kubernetes upgrade reviews the upgrades group.

Opinion (reading of the trigger list): the document does not say its five triggers are complete; when an overlay edit changes a limit other services share, as api's replica count does with PostgreSQL's connections, treating it as reaching past one service follows the worked example.
